title: EVs are a poor choice for long commutes over 50 miles daily
body: As a retired teacher who's been driving for decades, I've gotta say that EVs aren't ready for prime time when it comes to long commutes. body: I've owned my fair share of cars over the years but none have been as reliable as my old 1985 Toyota Land Cruiser. title: No-Till Success in Year 2!
body: I'm thrilled to report that our soil is finally starting to show signs of improvement after switching to no-till last year. We've had fewer compaction issues and our soil moisture levels are staying higher, even during dry spells. My son helped me dig up some areas and the roots on our corn plants are amazing - deep and strong. It's been a lot of work getting here, but it feels like we're finally reaping the benefits of no-till.

brief.angle: a phone battery that dies by noon
brief.ptype: sharing a practical tip that worked

title: My phone's battery dies by noon - simple solution found!
body: I was getting so frustrated with my Samsung Galaxy's battery life. It would go from 100% to 0% by lunchtime every day. I tried cleaning the charging port and recalibrating it, but nothing seemed to work. Then I read that some phones can be too 'cool' about overheating when charged rapidly. So, I plugged my phone in at night instead of first thing in the morning, and voila - no more dead battery by noon! Now I get through the whole day without needing a charge.

title: Drought is killing my well water
body: I've been farming this land for over 40 years and never seen it so dry. My well has dropped 10 feet in just a few months, and I'm starting to worry that it'll run out completely. The county said they can't do anything about the drought, but what's the point of having all these new rules about conserving water if we don't have any to conserve? It's enough to drive an old man crazy.
